subject.title: fix(reef): bound legacy state file reads in doctor migration

question: For valid Reef legacy files that exceed an in-memory migration threshold, should Doctor stream and fully migrate them, or stop with a supported recovery/resume workflow that preserves the original state?
rationale: This choice defines the durable-data upgrade contract; the current patch chooses permanent migration failure for valid data without maintainer-visible approval or recovery behavior.

options.title: Stream the migration
options.body: Implement bounded streaming parsing and incremental SQLite import so valid large audit and replay history migrates without an unbounded allocation.

options.title: Define an explicit recovery workflow
options.body: If full migration is intentionally deferred, preserve the legacy files and provide a tested Doctor diagnostic and resumable operator action rather than treating size alone as an unrecoverable error.

recommendation.title: Stream the migration
recommendation.body: Implement bounded streaming parsing and incremental SQLite import so valid large audit and replay history migrates without an unbounded allocation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Reef migration ownership could not be attributed from the available read-only evidence.
